tldr: TeamCraft is a multi-modal multi-agent benchmark built on Minecraft featuring 55,000 procedurally generated task variants with multi-modal prompts, designed to evaluate generalization across novel goals, scenes, and unseen numbers of agents. Existing vision-language-action models face significant challenges, particularly in decentralized settings and when generalizing to out-of-distribution scenarios.
contributions: TeamCraft, a new multi-modal multi-agent benchmark with a large-scale dataset encompassing complex tasks across diverse generalization scenarios
Extensive experiments and analyses on state-of-the-art multi-modal multi-agent models, uncovering their strengths and weaknesses
Open-sourcing of the entire platform, training and evaluation code, model checkpoints, and training data
methods: The benchmark is built on Minecraft using a Gym-like environment with first-person RGB observations and inventory information. Tasks (building, clearing, farming, smelting) are specified via multi-modal prompts combining language instructions with three orthographic view images. A planner generates expert demonstrations by optimizing a cost function minimizing task completion time, idle actions, action dependencies, and redundancy. The dataset contains 55,000 unique task variants with demonstrations. Generalization is evaluated on hold-out conditions: novel agent counts (4 agents vs. 2-3 in training), unseen scenes, and task-specific exclusions such as novel block shapes, materials, crops, and furnaces. Both centralized and decentralized agent settings are supported.
results: TeamCraft-VLA achieved an average accuracy of 37% overall. Performance dropped notably under generalization conditions: novel scenes reduced accuracy to 27%, and novel agent counts (4 agents) reduced it to 22%. In decentralized settings, accuracy dropped from approximately 46% to 18%. Baseline models including OpenAI GRPO and DreamerV3 also showed limited generalization capabilities.
limitations: Existing models continue to face significant challenges generalizing to novel goals, scenes, and unseen numbers of agents. The benchmark is confined to Minecraft-specific tasks and mechanics. The study focuses primarily on vision-language-action models and may not capture the full spectrum of multi-agent collaboration approaches.
